translation_source: Samuel Butler, 1900. Project Gutenberg #1727 (source-texts/pg1727-butler-1900.txt). The only translation used; no other consulted for wording (Fagles, Lattimore, Wilson, Fitzgerald not read).

source_verification.method: Independent reconstruction of PG #1727 lines 741-1116, written to a rule devised for this Book and audited against the raw lines before being trusted, then diffed against the staged original-en. NOT a re-run of whatever produced the served file.
source_verification.rule: The translation body contains exactly 187 digit runs and, read in order, they are the sequence 1..187 with no repeats and no gaps, against 186 bracketed entries in PG's FOOTNOTES: list numbered to 187 (only 29 absent, and that gap is in Book III). The counts reconcile, so every digit run in the body is a footnote reference and Butler's body carries no digits of its own. The rule is applied POSITIONALLY - the k-th run removed must BE the k-th marker - so a stray body digit breaks the arithmetic instead of vanishing, which a pattern rule ('delete any digit run') would not catch.
source_verification.result: 35 of 35 paragraphs byte-identical, zero diffs; 4184 words compared word-for-word.
source_verification.audit: PG lines 741-1116: 0 indented lines, 0 [Illustration markers, 0 in-text Greek, 0 daggers, 0 underscores, 1 square bracket (Butler's own '[do not]' at line 802, kept by the staged file), 7 footnote markers (17-23) on 6 lines, 11 short standalone lines all verified paragraph-final. Two audit catches recorded: 'FOOTNOTES:' occurs twice in the file and the first (line 75) is the table of contents - anchoring on it makes the body empty and the relation vacuously true; and Book 2's markers are never preceded by a space, so the rule's whitespace clause is a no-op here.
source_verification.negative_controls: Joining a paragraph's lines with a space instead of a newline differs in 35 of 35 paragraphs; leaving the markers in differs in 5 of 35. The check is capable of failing.

word_counts.note: Screening signal only; not evidence of semantic completeness, in either direction. Book 2 sits far closer to 1.0 than Book 1 (0.9462) because it is a Book of speeches in plain argument with much less of the long Victorian sentence-chaining Book 1's narration carries. A near-1.0 ratio carries its own risk - that the rendering is a light touch-up rather than a real modernization - so two counter-checks are offered to the reviewer rather than claimed as proof: no paragraph is byte-identical to Butler (0 of 35), and all 22 of Butler's dead words and forms in this Book are gone with none replaced by a different archaism.

naming.decision: Greek forms per GLOSSARY.md (standing finding S1, settled at Book 1). Book 2 is the first Book drafted under it from the start rather than remapped afterwards.
naming.counts: Odysseus 17, Athena 8, Zeus 6, Eurycleia 2 - each matching the source's Ulysses 17, Minerva 8, Jove 6, Euryclea 2 exactly. Neptune, Mercury, Saturn and Diana do not occur in Book 2.
naming.not_mapped: Ops (B02-P025), Butler's Greek name for Eurycleia's grandfather - a man. A general Roman->Greek deity list carries 'Ops -> Rhea'; GLOSSARY.md's table is closed and does not.
naming.flagged: Ilius (B02-P002), Butler's own form for Ilion/Troy, kept as he spells it - and note he writes 'Troy' in this same Book at B02-P010, so both stand in one chapter. Mycene (B02-P007) is the woman, not the city, and is kept. Both put to the reviewer.

punctuation.standard: PUNCTUATION.md: typographic quotation marks and apostrophes throughout. Verified: zero ASCII apostrophes and zero ASCII double quotes in the candidate.
punctuation.quotation_balance: candidate 29 open / 28 close, identical to the source's 29 / 28.
punctuation.d4_preserved: Butler's unclosed quotation at B02-P006 into B02-P007 (Antinous's continuous speech) is reproduced exactly; it is the only unbalanced paragraph in either file. The inner single quotation round Penelope's own speech IS closed at B02-P006's end, which is Butler and not a slip.

base_text_defects: One. B02-P004 carries Butler's own square bracket, '[do not] hold back' (PG line 802), which the staged original-en keeps verbatim. It is Butler's bracket, not PG apparatus. The candidate drops the mark and keeps the words, with a colon introduced to carry the pointing - the package's first bracket of any kind, put to the reviewer for a ruling and for whether it should become a recorded rule. See continuity.md 'Base-text defects'.
glosses: One, at B02-P008: 'the Erinyes-the spirits of vengeance-to avenge her'. Three words at first use, folded into the sentence, on the Book 10 pilot's 'cubit -> roughly eighteen inches' model. The English alternative 'the Furies' is a Roman name and is not available to this edition.
